_comment: A filled-in manifest for scripts/build_report.py, trimmed to a few scenarios. Every key except title is optional; the script documents the full schema at the top. Take scenarios from the suite's -json output rather than retyping them, and trim assertion-framework noise (an 'Error:'/'Messages:' prefix, a stack trace) out of each detail so it reads as a sentence.
title: Archimedes E2E Suite
headline: Archimedes E2E Suite
lede: It builds the server from a checkout, starts an MQTT broker in its own process, applies a schema reconstructed from the statements in the server's PostgreSQL adapter, runs the binary, and then drives it the way its devices and its operators do.
Nothing is stubbed, and nothing is imported from the server's own packages — so what passes here is what the deployed binary does.

scenarios.doc: GET /health is a liveness check (README.md API table)

scenarios.name: health_serves_the_methods_it_advertises
scenarios.doc: the route answers the methods its own Allow header names, and no others
scenarios.detail: the route answers "GET, HEAD", but the handler rejects every method that is not GET, so a HEAD liveness probe is refused by a route that advertises it

scenarios.name: unknown_pump_history_is_an_empty_array
scenarios.doc: the history handler answers [] rather than 404: the repository never returns nil

findings.title: HEAD /health is refused by a route that advertises it
findings.body: Registering GET /health makes net/http route HEAD to the same handler and answer Allow: GET, HEAD, but the handler's own method check rejects anything that is not GET. A HEAD liveness probe gets 405 from a route that says it accepts it.

findings.title: Failed database writes were reported as successes
findings.body: The write helper closed its rows without reading them, and pgx surfaces a statement's execution error only through those rows, so a rejected INSERT or UPDATE returned nil and the event was lost with no trace. Fixed by using Exec.

run.caption: Provision a database the suite may drop the archimedes schema in. It owns the schema; you own the cluster.
Point it at a checkout and run. Exit 0 when every scenario passed, 1 when any failed, 2 when the environment could not be stood up.

determinism: It waits on what the server wrote, never on a timer. Every published event carries an e2e_case field naming the scenario; the contract says unknown fields are ignored, so it changes nothing the server does — but the processors log each payload verbatim, which gives the scenario one unambiguous line to wait for. The log reader is cursor-based: a wait consumes the line it matched, so a later scenario cannot match an earlier one's line.
